study.notes: STUDY: Derosa 2011 (Eur J Pharmacol 666:251-256), the full paper of the group's 2010 EASD abstract (Derosa, exenatide vs glimepiride added to metformin), reached through the institutional route; Tables 1 and 2 with their legends and Methods and Results sentences copied into work/fulltext/companion/derosa2011_exenatide_glimepiride_tables.txt; randomised single blind controlled study, 12 months, exenatide 5 ug twice daily titrated after 1 month to 10 ug twice daily (dose_mg 0.01 per injection) vs glimepiride 1 mg three times daily titrated to 2 mg three times daily, both added to metformin at the highest dosages; 111 enrolled (57 and 54, Table 1), 101 completed (52 and 49, Table 2 at 12 months), 10 withdrawals listed with reasons; n_tx and n_ctrl are the 12 month completers; the 2010 abstract gave 130 randomised and 111 completers, the paper's figures govern; Table 1 gives baseline mean (SD) per arm and Table 2 the 12 month mean (SD) per arm for weight, HbA1c, fasting glucose, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR (route arm_change_imputed_r, correlation 0.5, within arm and between arm significance marks in the row notes); adiponectin, TNF-alpha and hsCRP at 12 months are shown only in Fig. 1 (not captured), so adiponectin and TNF-alpha keep the per arm changes of the 2010 abstract (read as mean and SEM) with the Table 1 baselines, and hsCRP has no numbers; pct_weight_change -5.25 computed by the session from Tables 1 and 2: exenatide 100*(75.1-80.2)/80.2 = -6.36 percent, glimepiride 100*(80.5-81.4)/81.4 = -1.11 percent, corrected -6.36 - (-1.11) = -5.25; no funding or sponsor statement found in the captured text (industry_funded FALSE provisional); no endpoint hierarchy stated (prespecified FALSE)

rows.notes: Tables 1 and 2: HbA1c percent, baseline mean (SD) per arm (n 57 and 54) and 12 month mean (SD) per arm (n 52 and 49); both arms P < 0.01 vs baseline, no between group difference stated (Results 3.3)
Tables 1 and 2: fasting plasma glucose mg/dL, baseline and 12 month mean (SD) per arm; both arms P < 0.01 vs baseline, no between group difference stated

Tables 1 and 2: fasting plasma insulin uU/mL, baseline and 12 month mean (SD) per arm; exenatide P < 0.05 vs baseline and P < 0.05 vs glimepiride at 12 months (marks a, d); glimepiride rose, not significant
Tables 1 and 2: HOMA-IR, baseline and 12 month mean (SD) per arm; exenatide P < 0.05 vs baseline and P < 0.05 vs glimepiride at 12 months (marks a, d)

2010 abstract: adiponectin change at 12 months 1.5 ± 0.4 exenatide vs 0.8 ± 0.03 glimepiride ug/mL (± read as SEM), glimepiride ns vs baseline, P < 0.05 vs exenatide; the paper shows the 12 month values only in Fig. 1A (exenatide increase P < 0.05 vs baseline and vs glimepiride); baseline Table 1 mean (SD) 4.9 (1.1) vs 4.7 (1.0)

2010 abstract: TNF-alpha change at 12 months -0.7 ± 0.04 exenatide vs -0.2 ± 0.01 glimepiride ng/mL (± read as SEM, reductions recorded as negative changes), glimepiride ns vs baseline, P < 0.05 vs exenatide; the paper shows the 12 month values only in Fig. 1B (exenatide decrease P < 0.05 vs baseline and vs glimepiride); baseline Table 1 mean (SD) 2.3 (1.2) vs 2.4 (1.3)

rows.trial_id: EQW vs insulin glargine 26 week 2010 abstract
rows.notes: second abstract in the group: exenatide once weekly 2 mg vs insulin glargine titrated to target, 26 weeks, open label, 456 subjects, per arm n not given; HbA1c primary endpoint, treatment difference -0.16 (SE 0.07) percentage points, p=0.017; body weight -2.6 (SE 0.2) kg vs +1.4 (0.2) kg, difference -4.0 (0.3) kg; pct_weight_change -2.86 computed at reconciliation as 100 x -2.6 / 90.9 (the pooled baseline weight 90.9 kg given in the abstract), arm change not placebo corrected; hsCRP, total cholesterol, triglycerides and ALT changes described as small but significant without numbers (no variance); design consistent with DURATION-3 (identification from the design, not stated in the abstract; the Lancet paper is not open access and was not captured); industry sponsored exenatide once weekly programme. STUDY notes of the Derosa trial do not apply to this row

json.design: two trials in one group: Derosa 2011 (randomised single blind, exenatide vs glimepiride added to metformin, 12 months, 111 enrolled, 101 completed) and a 26 week open label randomised trial of exenatide once weekly vs insulin glargine (456 subjects, abstract only)
json.reason: companion full paper of the Derosa abstract reached through the institutional route (Eur J Pharmacol 2011); its tables replace the abstract's per arm changes for HbA1c, fasting glucose, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR and supply baselines for adiponectin and TNF-alpha; the exenatide once weekly abstract row is unchanged

rob.justification: S (full paper): randomised without a stated method or concealment (D1); single blind (D2 some concerns); 10 of 111 withdrew with reasons listed, completers analysed (D3 low); laboratory outcomes (D4 low); no registration or protocol cited (D5)

doubts: the abstract's 130 randomised and 111 completers do not match the paper's 111 enrolled and 101 completed; the paper governs
the imputed change route pairs the enrolled baseline (n 57 and 54) with the completer 12 month values (n 52 and 49)
adiponectin and TNF-alpha changes come from the abstract because the paper gives the 12 month values only in a figure
